summary: Correct and within the rules, but the expected gain is about 0.3% on the geomean against a CI of at least +/-1.5%, so a neutral headline is what the run will most likely show. Run it once with no companions, and judge it from the profile's kernel table (the five replaced kernels against the one fused kernel), not from the speedup alone.
justification: Mechanism: on master the attention front runs five launches between the qkv GEMM and FA3 in the scored (kv_scale == 1) path: FusedQKNorm, k.to(FP8), v.to(FP8) on a strided slice of qkv, store_cache and q.view(T,16,64).to(FP8). Fusing them into one Triton kernel is plausible, and it is the same shape of fusion that gave attention_decode 1.127x. Size of the prize: at T=753 these kernels move only about 1.7 MB of q/k plus 0.2 MB of v in and about 1 MB of FP8 out. That is roughly 1 us of DRAM time, so nearly all the saving is launch and inter-kernel gaps inside the graph, about 1.5-3 us per kernel removed, or 5-10 us per shape. The hypothesis says 10-15 us, which is on the optimistic side. FINDINGS gives only the top three kernels per shape for master (Marlin MoE 45-66%, the nvjet GEMMs, FA3 on full layers). The only full per-kernel profile on disk (8a2df1fde4f54a7e) is the starter calibration and does not apply. So no measured number backs the 10-15 us. Direction and shapes: the expected directions agree with TASK.md. turn_1 (46x sliding at ~1080 us, 16x full at ~1435 us) gains about 0.5-1% on its load, turn_4 about 0.2%, first_turn about 0.05%. Each load counts equally in the geomean, so the problem-level gain is about 0.25-0.4%, well inside the +/-1.5% interval. Even turn_1's per-shape gain sits at or under the per-shape noise. The sister decode_layer cache-store-fused-fp8-cast was neutral on every shape, which fits launch savings not showing at this scale. Weakest link: the payoff is close to the resolution floor of the measurement. Exact numerical parity is the other weak spot: the hypothesis assumes FusedQKNorm applies norm and then RoPE in fp32 with a single bf16 rounding at the end. If FusedQKNorm rounds to bf16 between norm and rope, the fused kernel will differ by one ULP in places. That is harmless under the 8% cache bound and the attention bound, but it would break the pre-submit 'bitwise equal' check the change itself specifies, so read the FusedQKNorm source before trusting that check.
confounders: sglang-pipeline-parity (the only landed hypothesis): this change replaces part of its attention front, so the interaction is the change itself, not a confounder. Nothing else landed touches the pre-FA3 launch sequence. moe-align-side-stream is neutral and not on master, and its side-stream fork comes after attention, so it cannot overlap or compete with the new kernel.
interference: No companion is warranted. The problem is resolution, not attribution. An ab-revert has nothing to revert: the only landed item is the base whose kernels are being replaced. An ab-tune of the parity path would not change these five launches. A control that isolates one sub-change, such as fusing only the casts and store_cache while keeping FusedQKNorm, splits an effect of about 0.3% that is already below the interval into two smaller ones. Both arms would come back neutral, which spends quota without making the result easier to read. The result can be read without companions as follows. In the okc profile for the run, compare the new kernel's time and the attention-front span against the five parity kernels' summed time on the turn_1 shapes. If the fused kernel is shorter by a few us, the mechanism is confirmed even with a flat headline. If the fused kernel is slower than FusedQKNorm alone (per-row programs with poor occupancy at T=753), that explains a regression. Grab the parity kernel times from master's profile, or from the parent job's .txt if it has more than the top three, so the comparison is like for like.
rules_flags: No violation found. Queries are rounded to FP8 E4M3 as FA3 does, the cache stays FP8, the cos|sin table is a weight-independent constant built in prepare (not derived from data), the attention keys are untouched, and nothing host-syncs.
Keep the store with no reserved-slot skip: parity calls store_cache(..., reserved_skip_index=-1) because slot 0 is a live row here. The fused kernel must write every cache_loc, including 0.

The page_size=64 test relies on k_cache being contiguous [pages, page_size, 2, 64], so view(-1, 2, 64)[cache_loc] addresses the flat row. That holds for the given layout. Write through a view of the same storage, never a copy.

Keep the kv_scale != 1 path (some tests use 1/64) dividing after the bf16 rounding, as parity does. Load k_scale and v_scale from the device tensors inside the kernel, never with .item(), which is a host sync during graph capture.
Allocate q_fp8 from shapes only. Triton JIT compile happens on the warm-up call, outside capture, and counts toward the 15-minute run budget.
open_questions: Does FusedQKNorm round to bf16 once after norm+rope, or once after norm and again after rope? This decides whether the pre-submit check can be bitwise.
What are master's actual per-kernel times for FusedQKNorm, the three casts and store_cache at T=753? FINDINGS lists only the top three kernels, so the 10-15 us estimate has no measurement behind it.

fa3-contiguous-kv-gather (in flight) changes how the FA3 call reads the cache. If it lands first, this change needs a rebase so the fused store feeds whatever layout that branch expects, and the two should not be credited together without a rerun.
